Ask.description:
Questions a peko asks with its post (ADR-114 D1): a card that stays
open until someone answers it or the peko posts again. Carries no
authority — an answer is an ordinary post by whoever sends it.

for.description:
The member the card is for (an actor address on the roster), in
a group; `None` is anyone in the conversation. Clients show the

A file sent with a post (ADR-088). `path` is relative to the
receiving peko's workspace on the post itself; clients reading it
through `principal_log` get it absolute.

and no `path` (a host-local field). The channel keeps the bytes in
its file store under that digest; the receiving runtime pulls them
from the runtime that sent the post.

mime.description: The MIME type guessed from the name.

path.description:
Where the copy is. Empty when the copy is only in the channel's
file store (ADR-094).

sha256.description:
Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the bytes, for files kept in the
channel's file store (ADR-094).

caller.description:
Resolved caller identity as a typed `ActorRef` (ADR-039).
Populated on every event that flows through the request path so
the audit trail is attributable to a real subject — `User` /
`Principal` / `Public`. `None` only on legacy events that pre-date the
per-user attribution plumbing (issue #17) or on system-emitted
events with no caller context (use `ActorRef::User("local")` —
via `CallerContext::local().subject()` — or `ActorRef::Public`
for genuinely unauthenticated events, issue #26). For
security events with no caller context, prefer
`ActorRef::Public` over `None` so per-user audit queries can
still distinguish "unauthenticated security event" from "no
caller recorded" (issue #26 review feedback).

Local trust — no token provided.
Allowed only on the Unix socket and the Windows named pipe.
pekohub-issued JWT (short-lived).
Long-lived programmatic key.

AuthHeader.description: Authentication header appended to every request.

AuthenticatedRequest.description:
Authenticated request envelope (ADR-034).

New clients wrap their `RequestPacket` in this envelope.
Old clients send bare `RequestPacket`s, which deserialize with
`auth = AuthCredential::None` when parsed as this type.

oneOf.description:
Execute an agent message and stream the response — retired in
the principal-as-single-actor migration (audit C4). The legacy
Execute path went through `StatelessAgentService` directly,
bypassing `PrincipalManager` permission checks, session
creation, and root-agent routing. All chat traffic is now
routed through `PrincipalSend` (one-shot) or
`PrincipalSendStream` (streaming) — both go through
`PrincipalManager::receive` and produce principal-scoped
sessions and audit trails.
Execute a tool synchronously with the calling principal's
identity and session attribution (ADR-061, ADR-066). The synchronous counterpart of
the retired `AsyncSpawn` packet (removed 2026-09-27 with the
dead IPC async-spawn path, ADR-063 (dead IPC path)): same
server-side attribution (the principal is
resolved from `session_key`, its registered catalog is
derived from it server-side — never carried on the wire), but
the handler awaits the result and returns it as
`ResponsePacket::ToolExecuted` instead of a receipt. This is the
callback surface for agent-authored workflow processes
(`sdks/python/peko_workflow`).

`run_token` (phase 2b, ADR-061 D6): the `PEKO_RUN_TOKEN` a
`Workflow` spawn injected into the calling process. When
present it must validate against the daemon's in-memory
registry AND name this packet's `session_key` / principal —
unknown, expired, or mismatched tokens fail closed. When
absent, the pre-2b local-transport trust applies unchanged.

run_token.description:
Optional workflow run token; additive in phase 2b (older
clients never send it, older daemons ignore unknown fields).

Request graceful daemon shutdown

Run system doctor

Query the in-memory audit log for events emitted this
session (ADR-046). For historical events that pre-date the
current daemon process, the CLI falls back to reading the
JSONL file directly via `peko audit tail` — the IPC query
only sees the ring buffer. The CLI's `peko audit list`
subcommand is the primary user of this packet.

event_type_prefix.description:
Optional filter: only return events whose `event_type`
starts with this prefix (e.g. `"cron."`).

limit.description:
Maximum number of entries to return (newest first). The
daemon's ring buffer is bounded (10k entries); requests
above the cap are clipped by the ring buffer.

principal.description:
Optional filter: only return events whose `details.principal_name`
matches (or whose caller is a `ActorRef::Principal` with
this id). The `peko audit tail --principal` flag uses this.

oneOf.description: List all loaded Principals.

Look up a single Principal by name. Returns `ResponsePacket::PrincipalGet`
on hit, or `ResponsePacket::Error` with `principal_not_found` on miss.

Create a new peko (ADR-105). The daemon lays down its folder,
registers it, and schedules its first turn
(`principal::provision`); the caller owns it. `peko create` and
Peko Desktop both send this.

`model_id` is the configured model the principal pins at
creation. It is required: every principal must be created with

accept_setup.description:
The caller showed the seed's setup steps to the person and
they accepted them (ADR-104). A seed that carries setup steps
is refused with `[setup_not_accepted]` and the steps unless
this is true: the new peko runs them on its first turn, as
the owner's OS user.

seed.description:
A seed's TOML text (ADR-060), e.g. downloaded from PekoHub: the
new peko grows from it with a fresh identity, owned by the
caller. `model_id` and `description` override the seed's.

seed_path.description:
A seed file on this computer, read by the daemon, for a seed
too large to travel in one request. Only an operator caller
may name one; ignored when `seed` is given.

oneOf.description:
Load (or no-op when already loaded) a principal that exists on
disk into the daemon's in-memory manager. Used by
`peko principal create` when the daemon is already running:
the CLI materializes the workspace locally, then asks the
daemon to pick it up so the cron engine (which enumerates

Update an existing Principal's mutable config. All fields
except `name` are optional; omitted fields keep their current
values. Requires `ManageSettings` permission on the principal.

avatar.description:
An emoji or short monogram; `""` clears it
(`principal::config::validate_avatar`).

Remove a Principal and delete its workspace/data. Requires
`ManageSettings` permission on the principal.

Enumerate credentials in the vault. The optional `namespace`
and `kind` filters restrict the listing; missing filters match

Replaces the pre-RP3A provider-keyed `CredentialList`. The
desktop's `useCredentialList` (Tauri `credential_list`
command at `peko-desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/settings.rs:301`)

Fetch the full record for one credential (id, namespace, name,
kind, metadata, timestamps). The `material` field is NOT
included — use [`RequestPacket::CredentialGetMaterial`] for

Fetch the secret material for a credential. Audit-logged on

Free-form caller-supplied justification. Logged at INFO
alongside the credential id so an audit trail ties the
reveal back to its purpose.

endpoint answered. Replaces the pre-migration `CredentialTest`:
validation now happens at the model level (base URL + wire
format + credential), mirroring
`providers::validator::Validator::test`.

How a ChatGPT sign-in is going. `pasted_url` hands it the

Insert or overwrite a credential at `(namespace, name)` with
the given material. The vault assigns a fresh UUID on insert
and returns it in the reply; on overwrite the existing
credential at the slot is replaced (a new id is generated

supplied, every catalog entry that previously referenced the

Raw secret string from the caller. Wrapped in

Remove a credential by `id`. Powers the desktop's
`credential_delete` Tauri command; the CLI's
`peko credential delete <id>` writes the vault directly.
Mirrors `Vault::delete_credential`.

(the default), the handler refuses to delete a credential
referenced by one or more configured models and emits
`ResponsePacket::Error` with code `credential_in_use` so the

Enumerate every rotation binding currently configured in the

Fetch one binding by slot key. Returns `None` if no binding

slot. `strategy` is one of `round_robin` (today's only honored

Remove a binding by slot key. Returns `Ok(true)` if a binding

Re-read the model catalog and the credential vault from
disk. Sent by `peko model {add,remove}` and
`peko credential {set,delete}` so the long-running daemon
observes CLI mutations without a restart.

The chat models an endpoint offers, read from the endpoint

Read the principal's current quota status (used + limits +

oneOf.description:
Soft-stop the run bound to a (principal, peer) thread.

The stop complement to `PrincipalSend`/`PrincipalSendStream`:
the server resolves the peer's child session, fires the run's
cancel token (the agentic loop exits at the next iteration
boundary), posts a `⏹ stopped by user` marker to the peer's DM
channel, and leaves a stop-context note in the session inbox
for the next run. `peer: None` means the principal's owner
thread. The server enforces the same privacy rule as
`PrincipalLog` (`caller == peer || caller == principal.owner`).
Idempotent: no in-flight run ⇒ `Done { success: false,
error: "no running turn…" }` so the CLI can print a notice and
exit 0.

main.description:
Stop the turn in the peko's main session instead of a
conversation (ADR-104 D5): its first-turn setup, its
keepalive, or scheduled work. Owner only; `peer` is ignored.
A stopped first turn is over: it is not run again.

oneOf.description:
The approval requests waiting for a principal's owner (ADR-078 D7).
Owner (or operator) only.

How a peko's first turn is going (ADR-104 D4): whether it is
still setting itself up, what it has done so far, and its setup
report once written. Owner (or operator) only.

Run a peko's setup steps again (ADR-106): a setup turn that
checks each step and carries out the ones that do not work yet.
Owner (or operator) only. Answers `done`; `success: false` when
the peko lists no steps, a setup turn is already scheduled, or it
is still on its first turn.

The owner's decision on approval request `id`: approve (with
`always`, also add an always-allow rule to `POLICY.md`) or deny.
The owner's own action — the desktop's buttons, `peko approve` /
`peko deny` — never a message a model reads. Owner (or operator)
only.

A peko's secrets and the secret requests waiting for its owner
(ADR-116 D3): names only, never values. Owner only, local callers
only. Answered with `SecretList`.

The owner's value for secret request `id` (a `sec_…` id, or the
name of a waiting request), or for a new peko secret named `id`
when none waits (ADR-116 D3). The value goes to the vault and is
in no response. Owner only, local callers only. Answered with
`SecretDone`.

The owner declines secret request `id`. Owner only, local callers
only. Answered with `SecretDone`.

Remove peko secret `secret`. Owner only, local callers only.
Answered with `SecretDone`.

One thing a viewer asks of a peko's browser (ADR-119 D4–D6):
`state`, `frame`, `control`, `input`, `open`, `stop` for peko
`name`; or, with no peko, `status` (is there a browser to start)
and `install` (download the runtime's own). Owner only, local
callers only. Answered with `BrowserResult`.

Whether a peko is using this computer's screen, doing what, and
whether the owner's hand paused it (ADR-123 D5), with the
system's grants. Peko Desktop asks while it runs, to show its
indicator. Local callers only. Answered with `ComputerResult`.

**Let it continue** (ADR-123 D2): lift the pause the owner's input
put on the run using the screen, and wake its session. Local
callers only. Answered with `ComputerResult`.

**Stop** (ADR-123 D5): end the run using the screen, wherever it
runs (a conversation, cron, the keepalive). Local callers only.
Answered with `ComputerResult`.

Ask the system for the grants `Computer` needs (ADR-123 D5): on
macOS, opens the Screen Recording and Accessibility prompts for the
app that started the engine. Local callers only. Answered with
`ComputerResult`.

Recent turns of a peko that changed files, newest first (ADR-117):
those in `channel` when given, or with `dm`, in the DM of `peer`
(the caller when absent) as `principal_log` resolves it. Owner
only, local callers only. Answered with `TurnChanges`.

Undo turn `turn`'s file changes (ADR-117 D3). Owner only, local
callers only. Answered with `TurnUndone`.

Read a peer's conversation thread with a Principal.

This is the read complement to `PrincipalSend`. There is no
`peko session` CLI command (ADR-042): peers only ever see their
own thread, the owner sees their own by default, and any
other-thread read by the owner requires `peer` to be set
explicitly. The server enforces the privacy check (`caller ==
peer || caller == principal.owner`) plus the principal's `Chat`
grant before returning anything.

author.description:
Optional exact author filter (the raw channel-log author —
a peer ActorRef wire form or the principal's id).

cursor.description:
Opaque pagination cursor from a previous `PrincipalLog`
response's `next_cursor`. `None` reads the latest page.
Malformed cursors and cursors bound to another thread are
rejected with `bad_cursor`.

limit.description: Cap on number of messages returned (default 50, max 1000).

query.description:
Optional case-insensitive substring filter on message text.
Applied while paging (the daemon keeps walking older pages
until the page fills or the log is exhausted).

since_secs.description: Only messages newer than `now() - since_secs` are returned.

oneOf.description:
What a peko's visitors reach (ADR-113), for a sharing screen:
`[visitors]` and each person's own section of its `ACCESS.toml`,
the MCP servers it has, and the people it has talked with. Owner
only. Answered with `PrincipalAccess`.

Replace what visitors reach: `visitors` for everyone, and
`people` as the whole set of per-person sections (one left out is
removed). The file keeps its comments and `own` settings; nothing
is written unless the result is valid. Owner only. Answered with
`PrincipalAccess` as the file now is.

Follow everything a peko posts in its one-to-one conversations
(owner only): one `PrincipalSentAppended` per post, naming whom it
went to, with `Heartbeat` ticks between. For a script that
relays a peko's conversations to another service, so a message
the peko sends later (after its owner approves a request, say)
reaches the person too. `since` (RFC 3339) first replays the
peko's posts newer than it, oldest first; without it the stream
starts now. No `Done`: it ends when the client goes away.

Watch a peer's conversation thread with a Principal: replay
`Posted` events newer than `since_cursor`, then stream new
messages live.

The privacy-checked sibling of `ChannelEventsWatch` (ADR-042):
the server resolves `(name, peer)` to the peer's DM channel and
enforces the same rule as `PrincipalLog` (`caller == peer ||
caller == principal.owner`, plus the `Chat` grant). The
response is a stream of `PrincipalLogAppended` packets
interleaved with `Heartbeat` ticks (every
`HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECS`) so a quiet thread never trips the
client's per-packet idle timeout. No `Done` on close — the
stream ends when the client disconnects or the daemon shuts
down.

`since_cursor` reuses the log command's line-number cursor:
only rows with line number greater than the cursor replay.
`None` replays the whole thread.

since_cursor.description:
Replay seed — rows strictly newer than this line-number
cursor. `None` replays from the start.

actor.

`peko.toml` so the change survives daemon restart. Delegates

`peko.toml` so the change survives daemon restart. Delegates
to `TunnelDispatcher::set_instance_exposure` to publish an

supplies the desired `scope` (one or more `Permission` values)
and the TTL in seconds. The runtime returns the encoded token
plus its claims so the CLI/desktop can render the share URL.

an unknown `jti` is a no-op (returns success).

Create a new group channel owned by `creator_name` (DMs are
opened by `ChannelSend`, ADR-082).

(e.g. `group:<slug>`), validated by the handler via
`ChannelId::parse`. Serde-defaulted so pre-Phase-2 clients
decode as `None` (the store mints a fresh `chan_<8 base36>`).
Add `invitee_name` to `channel` (invited by `inviter_name`).

Post a message to `channel` from `sender_name`. `parent` is
the optional task_id of the message being replied to.

caller's own attribution identity is derived server-side from
the connection (`CallerContext::attribution_subject`).
`sender_name` is `None` ("speak as my own identity") or a

ADR-114 D1, D5: the post answers the questions of the post
`answers.to` (a root post: `parent` is refused with it).

attachments.description:
ADR-094: files to send with the post, as absolute paths on
this host; only the local user may attach. Each is copied into
the channel's file store; in a conversation with anyone on
another runtime or the Hub the bytes cross PekoHub, at most
10 MB a file and 25 MB a message.

model.description:
ADR-097 D2: a configured model of the peko's host to answer
this post with, recorded on the post (`Posted.model`). Only the
local user may set it; the host honours it only for the peko's
owner.

react.description:
ADR-126 D1: an emoji reaction on the post `react.to` instead
of a message; `text` and `parent` are ignored with it.

reply_to.description:
ADR-126 D6: the `msg_id` of the post this replies to, in place
of the line-number `parent`.

oneOf.description:
List events for `channel` since `since` (None = from start).

ADR-057: the reader's identity is derived server-side from the
connection (`CallerContext::attribution_subject`) — local and
pekohub JWT callers are always membership-gated as themselves;
API-key callers carry no user identity and stay ungated
(matching their previous no-requester posture).

author.description:
Search mode: exact `Posted` author match (wire form, e.g.
`user:alice`).

before.description:
Line-number cursor bounding the tail read from above
(events strictly older than this line). Ignored unless
`tail` is set.

query.description:
Search mode: case-insensitive substring match on `Posted`
text. When `query` or `author` is set, the daemon runs
`ChannelPort::search` (backward filtered scan; `tail` acts
as the match cap, `before` as the scan anchor) instead of
peeking.

tail.description:
Tail-read mode: return the newest `tail` events at or before
`before` instead of the full forward walk from `since`.
Maps to `ChannelPort::peek_tail`. When absent the legacy
forward `since` semantics apply.

oneOf.description:
PR-2b: subscribe to live events for `channel`. The daemon
replays events from `since` (None = from start) as a series of
`ChannelEventReceived` packets, then holds the connection open
and forwards new events as they arrive (signalled by the
dispatcher after `append_remote_event` succeeds). The stream
closes when the client disconnects or the daemon shuts down.

Wire-compatible with the chat's `PrincipalSendStream` shape
(request → stream of packets → `Done` on close) so the
desktop Tauri backend can reuse the existing stream-forwarding
path that already emits `peko-stream` events for the chat.

ADR-057: the reader's identity is derived server-side from the
connection — same caller-derived membership gate as
`ChannelPeek`.
List members of `channel`.
List channels where `principal_name` is a member.

Remove `principal_name` from `channel` (operator callers;
answers `channel_left`), or, with no `principal_name`, the
caller themself — a person leaving a group (answers
`channel_member_left`).

Copy a Runtime-tier channel into the Shared tier (PR-3d).
Authority gate (`channel:write_shared`) is enforced by the
daemon handler; the in-process CLI fallback path performs
the same check via `RuntimeAuthority`.

A channel's kind, name, members, and how each peko hosted here
wakes in it (ADR-082). Members only, like `ChannelPeek`.

Open, or find, the local user's DM with the peko named by `hub_id`,
hosted on another runtime (ADR-090 D2). `hub_id` is its PekoHub ID
or `@owner/name`; the answer's `hub_id` is always the ID. The
runtime resolves it through PekoHub — with `token`, the caller's
PekoHub access token, when given (used for that one request and
never stored), else with the runtime's own proof, which PekoHub
answers as the runtime's person — and invites it over the tunnel.
Then post and read with `channel_post` / `channel_peek` /
`channel_events_watch`. Local callers only. Answered with
`channel_remote_dm_opened`.

Open, or find, a DM with another person, whose PekoHub account is
`account` (ADR-095 D6). The first time, the person gets a message
request; posts wait in this copy until they accept. Local callers
only; answered with `channel_person_dm_opened`.

name.description: What to call them here until their runtime says.

oneOf.description:
This runtime's person's DMs with other people (ADR-095 D6). Local
callers only; answered with `channel_person_dms_result`.

This runtime's person's DMs with pekos on other runtimes, the ones
opened here and the ones that followed them from their other
computers (ADR-090, ADR-095 D5). Local callers only; answered with
`channel_peko_dms_result`.

The people asking this runtime's person to DM (ADR-095 D6), newest
first. Local callers only; answered with `channel_dm_requests_result`.

Answer a DM request (ADR-095 D6): `accept`, `decline`, or `block`.
Accepting opens the DM and tells the asker's runtime; declining and
blocking tell nobody. Local callers only; answered with
`channel_person_dm_opened` on accept, else `Done`.

Block (`blocked: true`) or unblock a person by PekoHub account
(ADR-095 D6). Local callers only; answered with
`channel_blocked_people`.

The people this runtime's person blocked. Local callers only;
answered with `channel_blocked_people`.

Scroll-back in a DM with a remote peko (ADR-091 D4): the page of
posts before `before` (a `msg_id`), from the peko's host. Not
stored on this runtime. Local callers only; answered with
`ChannelHistoryPage`.

The models the peko in `channel` — this account's DM with one of
its pekos on another runtime — can answer its owner with, from the
peko's host (ADR-097 D1). Local callers only; answered with
`ChannelPekoModelsResult`.

The approval requests waiting for you, the owner of the peko in
`channel` — this account's DM with one of its pekos on another
runtime — from the peko's host (ADR-099 D1). Local callers only;
answered with `ChannelPekoApprovalsResult`.

Your decision on approval request `id` of the peko in `channel`,
applied by its host as `approval_decide` (ADR-099 D2). The owner's
own action — the desktop's buttons — never a message. Local
callers only; answered with `ApprovalDecided`.

One thing you ask of the browser of the peko in `channel`, your
DM with a peko on another of your computers (ADR-119 D6): `verb`
is `state`, `frame`, `control`, `input` or `open`, carried out by
its host. Local callers only; answered with `BrowserResult`.

The groups inviting this runtime's person (ADR-092 D2), newest
first. Local callers only; answered with `ChannelInvitationsResult`.

The groups this runtime's person joined from other runtimes
(ADR-092 D2). Local callers only; answered with
`ChannelPersonGroupsResult`.

Join a group by its invite link, or a public one by its ID
(ADR-092 D5): PekoHub says where it lives, and its home decides.
Local callers only; answered with `ChannelGroupJoined` once the
request is on its way (the group arrives with the home's roster).
With `peko` (a name or local id of a peko the caller owns), that
peko joins, for itself (ADR-098 D2); without, the person does.

Register a group with PekoHub, or change who may find it
(ADR-092 D5), at its home and as its owner peko. Only that peko's
owner; answered with `ChannelGroupRegistered`.

Make an invite link to a registered group good for `days` (default
7, at most 30), or with `revoke` stop every link (ADR-092 D5). As
for `ChannelGroupRegister`; answered with `ChannelGroupLinkResult`.

Set what starts a turn for `principal_name` in a group
(`human` / `mention` / `off`, ADR-082 D3). Groups only — a DM
always wakes on human posts — and only the peko's owner.

ADR-101: read a group's board, or change it with `op` first. The
change is posted as `sender_name` (a peko the caller operates) or,
when absent, as the caller. Groups only. Answered with
`ChannelBoardResult`.
The posts in `channel` not yet delivered to a member on another
runtime (that runtime has been away since, e.g. asleep), by
`msg_id`. Members only. Answered with `ChannelUndeliveredResult`.

ADR-111 D3: show a code that adds a device to this account (a
phone scans it, another computer types it): single use, ten
minutes. Local callers only; this computer must be on its account's
list. Answered with `DeviceCodeShown`.

ADR-111 D3: join this computer to its account's devices with a code
shown on a device already on them. Answers `done` once the device
list has this computer on it (up to two minutes). Local callers only.

ADR-111: this account's devices, whether this computer is on them,
and what waits for the owner about the account (owner changes,
pekos' new identities, contacts' devices that start over). Local
callers only. Answered with `DeviceListResult`.

ADR-125 D9: how this computer connects to its other computers and
people's, and the path to each (`direct`, `relay`, `waiting`,
`offline`). Local callers only. Answered with `NetworkStatusResult`.

ADR-125 D9: set any of the `[network]` link settings; writes
`runtime.toml` and applies them at once (starts or stops the
listener, closes links no longer admitted, tells peers whether
this computer takes relayed frames). An absent field is left as it
is; an empty `direct_listen` goes back to the default. Local
callers only. Answered with `NetworkStatusResult`.

ADR-125 D9: dial a computer's known addresses now (every one's,
without `runtime_id`), without waiting for the backoff. Local
callers only. Answered with `Done`.

ADR-112: the code of an identity as this computer holds it, to
compare with its owner's: `account`, `user:hub:<id>`,
`peko:hub:<id>`, or one of your pekos by name or id. Local callers
only. Answered with `IdentityCodeResult` (`code` absent when this
computer holds no identity for it yet).

ADR-111 D4: remove a device from the account (by its id, or a
phone's Hub id); every computer stops acting on it. Local callers
only. Answers `done`.

ADR-111 D6: decide one of `device_list`'s `security` requests.
Local callers only. Answered with `ApprovalDecided`.

ADR-108 D5: the person has seen `channel` up to a post. Name it by
`msg_id`, or give `at` (RFC 3339) for the newest post at or before
that time, which is what a client that shows a thread by time
knows. Exactly one of the two. Moves their read mark forward (never
back) and tells their other computers. Local callers only. Answered
with `ChannelReadMarked`.

ADR-108 D5: the person's read mark and unread count in each of
their conversations. Local callers only. Answered with
`ChannelReadStateResult`.

BoardOp.description:
A change to a group's board (ADR-101), carried by the post that
makes it. The board is the fold of every op in the group's log; an
item's id is the `msg_id` of the post that added it.

Authority comes from the post's author, never from the op: who may
make which op is decided where the board is folded.

oneOf.description:
A new item, `open`. `for_member` names the member it is asked
of (a mention of that member).
The author takes the item: state `doing`.

check_at.description: RFC 3339; when the claimant looks at it again (D6).

oneOf.description: Move the item to `doing`, `blocked`, or `done`.
The claimant lets go: state `open`, no claimant, no check-in.
The item leaves the board.

BoardState.description:
What a board item is doing (ADR-101 D1). An item a `release` reopens
has no claimant; `open` is never set by an `update`.

BootState.description:
Genesis-pipeline boot state for a Principal (ADR-054).

Tracks how far a principal has progressed through the
creation/booting pipeline so `PrincipalManager::create`, `load`,
and the daemon's boot-time seeding share one state machine:

- `provisioned` — P0 done (workspace tiers, DID, config persisted);
  no creator definition has been recorded yet.
- `defined` — P1 done: `[identity]` / `[intent]` content (or a
  custom root prompt) is present.
- `genesis_pending` — P2 seeding done: the daemon has scheduled the
  one-shot genesis turn and the default keepalive job.
- `organized` — the genesis run finalized successfully; the trunk
  owns its cadence and boot no longer seeds its cron schedule.
  This records execution completion, not verified self-organization.

ChangedFile.description: One file a turn changed, as shown.

path.description: Relative to the workspace when inside it.

oneOf.description: Channel creation. Fires once at the top of the event log.

A message authored by `author`. `parent` references the prior
message being replied to; `None` for the channel's first post.

answers.description:
ADR-114: a person's answers to a post's questions. Only a
person's post carries them; the post's `text` reads the same
answers. Omitted when absent.

ask.description:
ADR-114: questions a peko asks with this post. Only a
principal's post carries them. Omitted when absent.

attachments.description:
Files sent with the post (ADR-088), kept in the receiving
peko's workspace. Omitted when empty, so lines without
attachments are byte-identical to before.

board.description:
ADR-101: a change to the group's board. The post's `text` is
a readable line the runtime wrote from it, so clients and
runtimes that predate the board show the change as a post.
Omitted when absent, so other lines are byte-identical to
before.

model.description:
ADR-097 D2: a configured model id the author asks the
receiving peko to answer this one post with. Honoured only by
a peko's host for its owner, and only for a model enabled
there; everything else ignores it. Omitted when absent, so
lines without it are byte-identical to before.

msg_id.description:
Stable message id, assigned once by the posting store and
carried verbatim to every runtime's mirror (line numbers
differ between mirrors; this does not). `None` on lines
written before the field existed.

options.description:
Suggested replies (ADR-093): a few short answers a reader
may send instead of typing. Text only — a tapped option is
an ordinary post by whoever taps it and carries no
authority. Omitted when empty, so lines without options are
byte-identical to before.

react.description:
ADR-126 D1: an emoji reaction on another post. A post carrying
one is not a message ([`ChannelEvent::is_message`]): it wakes no
one, is not unread, and is left out of digests and reads. Its
`text` is a readable line the runtime wrote from it, and it is
written as a reply (`parent` set, `reply_to` empty), so a
runtime that predates this treats it as a reply that starts
nothing. Omitted when absent.

reply_to.description:
The `msg_id` of the message this post replies to — the
cross-runtime form of `parent`. Set by the posting store from
the parent line's own `msg_id`; `None` for root posts and for
replies to messages without an id.

via.description:
Attribution: the session slug path (e.g. `/user-a/reminder`)
of the posting agent within the author's principal. Written
verbatim — audit metadata only, NOT an authority claim; it
never feeds membership checks, responders, or reply
matching. Absent on lines written before this field existed
(serde defaults to `None`; `None` emits nothing on the wire,
keeping old peers byte-compatible).

oneOf.description:
A principal was invited / joined the channel. Append-only — a
subsequent `MemberLeft` carries the inverse.
A principal left (or was removed from) the channel.

Delivery receipt, runtime to runtime: the sender of this event
applied the envelopes `request_ids` it received for `channel`.
Transport only — never appended to a channel log. It rides the
same relayed `TunnelChannelEvent` envelope as channel events so
the hub needs no new message type.

ChannelGroupSummary.description:
A group's home and PekoHub registration in a `ChannelInfoResult`
(ADR-092 D1/D5).

home_here.description:
This runtime is the group's home: its settings, roster, PekoHub
registration and invite links are managed here.

hub_id.description: The group's PekoHub ID, once registered.

page.description: Its page on the website, once registered.

ChannelId.description:
Channel identifier. Opaque `String` newtype.

Conversation IDs and compatibility dispatch references (see [`ChannelKind`]):

| Wire form             | Kind       | Semantics                                          |
|-----------------------|------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `chan_<8 base36>`     | `Bare`     | Plain fire-and-forget post                         |
| `dm_<64 hex>`         | `Bare`     | Pair conversation post                            |
| `principal:<ref>`     | `Principal`| Resolve actor, provision pair DM, post             |
| `user:<id>`           | `User`     | Fire-and-forget note to a user                    |
| `visitor:<id>`        | `User`     | Fire-and-forget note to an anonymous visitor      |
| `group:<slug>`        | `Group`    | Fire-and-forget post to a group                   |

Bare ids are generated by [`ChannelId::generate`]; typed ids are
minted via [`ChannelId::for_principal`] / [`ChannelId::for_user`] /
[`ChannelId::for_group`]. [`ChannelId::parse`] accepts any of the
forms above. Actor references are dispatch inputs; new DM storage uses
opaque pair IDs. Old typed channel IDs remain readable. The inner field serializes directly to a JSON string
(no `#[serde(transparent)]` — the project doesn't use it, matching
`peko_subject::PrincipalId`).

ChannelPekoWake.description: One peko hosted on this runtime in a `ChannelInfoResult`.

ChannelPerson.description: One member of a channel in a `ChannelInfoResult`, as people read it.

aliases.description:
The other forms they appear as here: a remote peko's signing
`did:key`, a person's Hub address, a local id.

handle.description:
A person's PekoHub handle, when known (ADR-124): unique, where
names may repeat.

here.description: Hosted on this runtime (a peko here, or you).

name.description:
Their name, when known: a peko's name, a person's PekoHub
display name.

ChannelReadInfo.description: The person's read state in one conversation (ADR-108 D5).

peer.description:
A DM's other member, so a client can tell which conversation this
is (a peko by `local_id` or `hub_id`, a person by `hub_id`).

read.description: The newest post the person has seen, by `msg_id`.

unread.description: Posts after the mark that the person did not write.

Connection.description: ADR-125 D2: how this computer connects to other computers.

oneOf.description: Everything through PekoHub; the engine neither listens nor dials.
A direct link whenever one is up, PekoHub otherwise.
Direct links only; nothing of a conversation crosses PekoHub.

ConversationKind.description:
What a channel is (ADR-082 D1): a two-member pair conversation or a
group with a mutable roster. Set at creation, never changed, and
carried on the signed cross-runtime invite.

oneOf.description:
A pair DM: id `dm_<SHA-256>` of its two members' keys; the
roster never changes.
A `group:<slug>` / `chan_*` channel with a mutable roster.

Credential.description:
Full credential record returned by `CredentialGet`. Includes
metadata but NOT the secret material — use
[`ResponsePacket::CredentialMaterial`] for that.

CredentialRow.description:
One row of `CredentialsListed`. Redacted — never carries the
secret material. The full record (including metadata) is fetched
via `CredentialGet`; the material itself is only available via
`CredentialGetMaterial` (RP3A: audit-logged).

`id` is the credential's UUID. `namespace` and `name` together
identify the slot (`provider:openai / default`,
`mcp:analytics / default`, `oauth:myremote / default`, …).
`kind` is the lowercase snake_case spelling of
[`crate::common::vault::CredentialKind`] (`api_key`,
`bearer_token`, `oauth_token`, `basic_auth`, `private_key`,
`generic_secret`).

`last_tested_at` is an ISO-8601 UTC stamp from the most recent
`CredentialTest` against this credential; `last_tested_ok`
records the outcome. Both are `None` until the first test runs.

`is_referenced` / `referenced_by` (PR 3 / `feature/model-first-config`):
populated when the catalog has at least one `ModelConfig` whose
`credential_id` matches this row. `is_referenced` is the cheap
summary flag the desktop paints next to the credential name;
`referenced_by` carries the dependent `ModelSummary` rows so the
delete confirmation dialog can show jump links without a follow-up
`model list` round-trip. `#[serde(default)]` keeps the field
forward+backward compatible — old daemons that don't compute
references deserialize as `false` / `[]`, and old clients ignore
the fields on a new daemon.

DeferredToolsMode.description:
Per-provider tool-deferral policy (F29).

Some OpenAI-compatible providers delay-emitting tool calls until
the model's reasoning block closes (Kimi notably). The engine
loop's tool-call accumulator respects this via
`ProviderCompat::deferred_tools_mode`.

oneOf.description: Fire tool calls as soon as the adapter surfaces them.

Kimi-specific deferral: `tool_call_id` and `arguments` may
only land AFTER the trailing `reasoning` block closes. The
accumulator should not surface a `ContentBlock::ToolCall`
until `Done { stop_reason: ToolUse }` arrives.

DeviceInfo.description: A device on the account's list, as `device_list` reports it (ADR-111).

added_by.description: The device that added it (itself, for the first one).

id.description: Its key as a `did:key` (a computer's runtime id).

last_seen.description:
RFC 3339, to the minute: when a phone last asked this computer for
something.

path.description:
ADR-125 D9: how another computer is reached now (`direct`,
`relay`, `waiting`, `offline`). Absent for phones, this computer,
and from older engines.

DirectWith.description: ADR-125 D4: which computers this one links with.

oneOf.description: The computers on the owner's own device list.

Also every computer of another person, or hosting another person's
peko, that this computer seals to.

reported.description:
What the endpoint's own list says. Many lists say nothing but
the id.

suggested.description:
What the public models.dev catalog says, fetched when asked:
a suggestion for the person to accept or edit, never stored
unasked.

DmRequest.description:
A person's request to DM this runtime's person, waiting for their
answer (ADR-095 D6). It names only who asks; nothing goes back to the
asker until it is accepted.

account.description: The Hub account it is for.

channel.description: The pair id the DM will have.

name.description: The display name the asker's runtime gave, if any.

source_runtime.description: The runtime it came from: the asker's first route on accepting.

ExecutableDefinition.description:
A command-bearing manifest, retained verbatim so binds, arguments, and
malformed definitions remain visible without executing or loading them.

file_count.description: Payload files, excluding the inventory manifest itself.

Exposure.description:
Network exposure level for a Principal (persisted in
`peko.toml`).

This used to live in `peko_principal::config::Exposure` and was
imported by `auth::Resource::Principal` to fill the `exposure`
field. Moving it to `peko-auth` makes `Resource` self-contained
(no inbound dep from peko-auth to peko-principal) and lets
`peko-principal` (the future Phase 14 extraction) import it from
`peko_auth` without a cycle.

Registration visibility: local-only, registered private, or registered public.
Hub identity assignment is recorded separately in the runtime actor registry.

GroupInvitation.description:
A group's invitation waiting for the person's answer (ADR-092 D2),
kept on each of their runtimes until they accept or decline.

account.description: The Hub account it is for.

home_runtime.description: The group's home runtime, which sent it.

initial_members.description: The roster as the home sent it.

requested.description:
The person asked to join (with a link or a group's ID, or from a
new device, ADR-092 D4/D5); it waits for the home's roster, not
for an answer.

InitialMember.description:
One row of the `initialMembers` list on
[`crate::tunnel::TunnelChannelInvite`] (the source runtime's
fan-out of a channel invite to a remote runtime's hosting
runtime). Pairs a principal DID with the runtime that hosts it.

Wire shape:

```json
{"principalDid":"prin_alice"}
{"principalDid":"prin_bob","runtimeId":"did:key:zRuntimeB"}
```

`runtime_id: None` means the principal is local to the source
runtime — the receiver should land the row in
`members.json`'s local array. `runtime_id: Some(id)` means the
principal lives on a peer runtime and the receiver should
record a `RemoteMember` row.

`#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` on
`runtime_id` keeps the wire form minimal for the common
(single-runtime) case: a 4-line bootstrap envelope shrinks by
~22 bytes per local member. Verified by
[`initial_member_skips_none_runtime_id`].

InviteClaims.description:
The claims embedded in an invite token. All fields are required
(no `Option`s) — refusing a token for any missing field is part of
the security model: a token whose `scope` is missing entirely must
not silently mean "everything".

exp.description: Expiry instant (UTC). The verifier rejects tokens past this.

jti.description:
Unique token ID — used by the revocation set. A fresh UUID v4
per mint; the runtime's `InviteRevocationSet` is keyed on this.

owner_subject.description:
ActorRef this token is restricted to. The dispatcher's
`x-pekohub-user-id` header (or the resolved JWT `sub`) MUST
equal this value for the token to be accepted.

principal_did.description:
The runtime's DID for the principal this token grants access to.
(The recipient's runtime does NOT need to know this — the
runtime_checker uses it to disambiguate which principal the
token is for if the same owner owns multiple principals.)

principal_name.description: The principal name, also used as the dispatcher match key.

scope.description:
Permissions the token grants. The dispatcher currently only
enforces `Chat` (the only operation that crosses the tunnel),
but other permissions are recorded so the token can later be
used for finer-grained operations without a re-issue.

LaunchMode.description:
How this daemon was launched.

Used by the Status response so clients can tell who owns the running
IPC socket. `Headless` is the default for `peko daemon start` (CLI)
and any ad-hoc invocation; `Sidecar` is set by `peko-desktop`'s
supervisor so it can detect when a foreign daemon is already
holding the socket (and adopt it instead of spawning a competing
child). See ADR-043 §adoption.

`pub` (not `pub(crate)`) because `ResponsePacket::Status::mode`
is part of the public IPC wire envelope (`ipc::packet` is `pub`).

MemberProvenance.description:
P1.2 attribution: pairs a principal DID with its hosting runtime
id. `runtime_id: None` means the principal is local to the
receiving runtime; `Some(runtime_id)` means the principal is hosted
on a peer runtime that joined the channel via the cross-runtime
invite envelope.

The flat `ChannelMembership::members` list is the back-compat
surface; `MemberProvenance` is the richer shape that lets the UI
render local vs remote members distinctly. Pre-PR-3b consumers
that don't read `member_provenance` see no change to the wire
shape — the field uses `#[serde(default)]` and skips when empty.

ModelAddArgs.description:
Explicit model endpoint settings, matching `peko model add`.
Credentials are stored in the vault; optional metadata is user authored.

api_format.description:
API format: openai_completions, openai_responses, or anthropic_messages. Maps to
`ApiFormat::from_wire`.

base_url.description: Base URL for a custom model.

context_window.description: Optional user-supplied limits and metadata; no vendor defaults.

credential_id.description:
Reference an existing vault credential by id instead of
storing a new key. Mutually exclusive with `key`.

custom.description: Legacy compatibility flag, accepted without effect.

effort.description:
How hard the model thinks on every turn (`low` … `max`);
absent or `none` sends no effort.

effort_levels.description:
The levels the model takes, as its endpoint (or models.dev)
listed them, kept for changing the effort later.

key.description:
Store an API key in the vault immediately. Equivalent to
`peko credential set <id>` after the add. Rejected for keyless entries.

model.description: Exactly one wire model id. The vector shape is retained for IPC compatibility.

name.description: Configured id. Defaults to the wire model id.

requires_key.description:
Whether the custom model requires an API key.
Defaults to `true` when omitted.

template.description: Retired preset selector; present requests receive migration guidance.

ModelDiscoverArgs.description:
Arguments for `RequestPacket::ModelDiscover`: the endpoint, as for
`ModelAdd`, and the key to list with.

key.description: Not stored. Absent for keyless endpoints.

What is known about a model's limits and abilities. Every field is
optional: absent is "not said", not "no".

ModelPresetInfo.description: Legacy preset wire shape. ModelTemplates now returns an empty list.

api_type.description:
`"openai"` or `"anthropic"` — matches `ModelSummary::api_type`
and the underlying `ApiFormat` enum's snake-case wire ids.

base_url.description:

supply a deployment URL (e.g. `azure-openai`).

cache_read_per_million.description: USD per 1M cached input tokens read; `None` = input rate.

ModelSpec.description:
PR 1 / `feature/model-first-config`: IPC mirror of
`peko_providers::spec::ModelSpec`. Kept in this file (rather than
imported from `peko_providers`) so the wire shape is owned by the
IPC layer and can evolve independently. All fields use
`#[serde(default)]` so packets emitted by a pre-PR-1 daemon
deserialize cleanly into the new field set.

The mirror is intentionally one-way: the daemon reads `ModelSpec`
from `ModelConfig::spec` and projects it onto this struct. The
desktop never round-trips a `ModelSpec` back through IPC — edits
go through the catalog file (`peko model edit` / `peko model add`)
rather than the IPC.

decisions.description:
ADR-061 (D4): judgment-class model flag. Read by the
`ModelCall` built-in's judgment-mode gate; the desktop does
not consume it today.

ModelSummary.description:
Summary of an extension for IPC responses
Catalog-summary view of one configured model entry.

This is the canonical list-row shape for the model-first catalog
(`models.toml`). The wire field for the API format stays the short
form (`"openai"` / `"anthropic"`) so the desktop's existing
rendering code keeps working without a coord change; the runtime
translates to/from the catalog's `ApiFormat`
(`openai_completions` / `anthropic_messages`).

api_format.description:
Short wire id: `"openai"` or `"anthropic"`. The desktop's
existing renderer reads this field, so the on-wire value stays
stable; the runtime translates to/from the catalog's
`ApiFormat` (`openai_completions` / `anthropic_messages`).

base_url.description:
Base URL configured for this model. Empty for presets
where the user must supply a deployment URL (e.g.
`azure-openai`).

context_window.description: Maximum context length in tokens (input + output).

credential_id.description:
Reference to a credential in the vault. `None` means the model
does not require an API key (e.g. a local Ollama endpoint).

effort.description:
How hard the model thinks on every turn; absent sends no
effort (the provider's own default).

effort_levels.description:
The levels the model takes, as its provider listed them when it
was added; empty when not known.

enabled.description:
Catalog `enabled` flag. Disabled entries still appear in the
list so the desktop can render them greyed-out / at the bottom
of the models panel.

headers.description:
Optional extra HTTP headers (e.g. `OpenAI-Organization`).
Empty for most entries; non-empty for vendors that require a
tenant header.

is_local.description:
True iff the catalog entry has `requires_key = false` (local
model like Ollama). Surfaced to the desktop so it can hide
the "Add Key" CTA.

model_id.description:

user note attached to this entry. Surfaced on the IPC
`model.list` / `model.show` replies and (via the
`ModelList` builtin) to the parent agent so it can pick

spec.description:

descriptor (vision, audio, tools, streaming, thinking,
json_mode, pricing). `None` for entries written before
PR 1; the desktop falls back to `ModelSpec::default()` in
that case (text-only, no tools, no thinking, streaming on).
Field is skipped from JSON when absent so old daemons and
old desktop builds keep working against new packets, and
vice versa.

template_id.description:
Template/preset id this entry was seeded from. `None` for
fully custom entries.

ModelTemplateInfo.description: Legacy preset wire row, retained for decoding older IPC responses.

efforts.description:
Effort levels the model takes, lowercase, as the source names
them (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `none`, …). Empty
when thinking is only on or off.

ModelUpdateArgs.description:
Arguments for `RequestPacket::ModelUpdate`.

Every field except `id` is optional. Omitted fields leave the

spec.description:
Replace the capability descriptor (which inputs the model takes,

name.description: What they are called here, when known.

No runtime of theirs is known yet: they have not accepted, so
nothing written here has reached them.

PersonGroup.description:
Response sent from Daemon → CLI

Options of the question that were chosen; at most one unless the

PlanModelWire.description: A model a ChatGPT plan offers.

PrincipalDID.description: Thin wrapper around a DID string.

PrincipalId.description: Newtype wrapper for a stable principal identifier.

PrincipalLogMessage.description:
One immutable, consumer-visible text message in a `PrincipalLog`
page — the row type of `peko log`. Lives next to the packet that
carries it; the dedicated chat-log store crate was retired in
Phase 13 (the peer DM channels are the record now).

Wire shape is unchanged from the retired chat-log row type
(camelCase field names, same defaults/skips).

answers.description:
ADR-114: the person's answers to an earlier message's questions;
`text` reads the same answers.

ask.description:
ADR-114: questions the sender asks with the message. A client
shows the card open until an answer names it or the sender asks a
newer card; in a DM, also until the person posts again.

ADR-088 D3: files attached to the message, each `path` absolute
on the runtime's host.

The post's stable id (`msg_id`), the one a client names when it
answers the post's questions (ADR-114). `None` on old lines.

ADR-093: suggested replies the sender offered with the message.
A client shows them only while this is the conversation's last
message; a tap sends the option's text as an ordinary message.

reactions.description:
ADR-126 D1: the emoji on the message, each with who put it there.
Reactions are never rows of their own.

replyTo.description:
ADR-126 D6: the `msg_id` of the message this one replies to. A
client quotes it above the reply, except right after it.

Display name of the sender when it is the peko whose log is
being read (its own replies). `None` for every other actor —
they render by address.

PrincipalSummary.description:
Lightweight projection of a `Principal` for IPC list/show responses.

The runtime formerly returned `Vec<AgentSummary>` from its
`AgentList` IPC; after the principal-as-single-actor migration the
actor surface is `Principal`. `PrincipalSummary` is the canonical
wire-form shape for the post-migration `PrincipalList` /
`PrincipalGet` IPC variants — see audit finding C1.

avatar.description:
The peko's avatar: an emoji, or a short monogram
(`identity.avatar`, see [`config::validate_avatar`]).

boot_state.description:
Where the peko is in its first-turn pipeline (ADR-054). Anything
but `organized` means it is still setting itself up.

ProviderCompat.description:
Per-provider adapter hints (F29).

`ModelConfig::compat: Option<ProviderCompat>` carries the hints
resolved from the template at catalog construction time;
`ChatOptions::compat_override` lets callers override per-call.
Both default to `None` so pre-F29 wire shapes (OpenAI
`reasoning_effort`, Anthropic `thinking: {type, budget_tokens}`)
stay unaffected — adapters fall back to their F25 built-in
defaults when compat is unset.

multi.description: Whether more than one option may be chosen.

options.description: None (a free-text question) or 2–4 choices of one line each.

QuotaConfig.description:
Token + request-count limits for a principal.

All three limits are independent and optional. A `None` field
means "unlimited for this dimension" — the meter will not check
or trip on it.

budget_per_cycle.description:
Phase 3 of `feature/multi-model-subagents`: cycle-window
USD budget. The meter sums per-call cost alongside the
existing token / request counters; once the running total
exceeds this, `try_charge` rejects. `None` ⇒ uncapped.

cost_per_call_max.description:
Phase 3 of `feature/multi-model-subagents`: per-spawn cost
ceiling in USD. When `Some`, the spawn-time pre-flight
(`SubagentExecutor::execute_and_wait`) refuses any spawn
whose conservative cost estimate exceeds this. `None`
(default) ⇒ no per-call cap. `f64` because cost is
intrinsically fractional (cents/mtok arithmetic).

`Eq`/`PartialEq` removed from the derive above because
`f64` does not implement `Eq`; comparisons use
`approx_eq` helpers in tests.

QuotaCycle.description: Calendar-aligned reset cycle. All boundaries are UTC.

oneOf.description: Reset at the top of every UTC hour.

Reset at 00:00 UTC every day. **Default** — the most common
rate-limit cycle; `QuotaConfig::default()` picks this so an
unconfigured cycle still behaves sensibly.
Reset at 00:00 UTC every Monday (ISO week boundary).
Reset at 00:00 UTC on the 1st of every month.

QuotaState.description: Runtime counters for one principal's current quota window.

cache_creation_tokens.description:
Cumulative cache-creation input tokens in the current
window (tokens the provider charged for writing into its
prompt cache). Informational — not gated by any limit.
`serde(default)` for the same backward-compat reason as
`cache_read_tokens`.

cache_read_tokens.description:
Cumulative cache-read input tokens in the current window
(tokens the provider served from its prompt cache).
Informational — not gated by any limit. `serde(default)`
keeps state files written before this field existed
loadable (they deserialize as `0`).

cost_usd.description:
Phase 3 of `feature/multi-model-subagents` —
cumulative USD spend in the current window. `None` for
pre-Phase-3 state files (the meter treats absent as
`0.0`).

cycle.description:
Cycle that produced this window — copied from the config so
we can detect config drift on reload.

input_tokens.description: Cumulative input tokens consumed in the current window.

output_tokens.description: Cumulative output tokens consumed in the current window.

request_count.description: Cumulative LLM requests made in the current window.

window_end.description:
Window end (exclusive, UTC). When `now >= window_end` the
meter rolls forward.

ReactOp.description:
An emoji reaction (ADR-126 D1), carried by the post that makes it.
Who reacted is the post's verified author, never anything in the op.
The reactions on a message are the fold of every op in the log
(`peko_channel::reactions`).

emoji.description: One Unicode emoji (a single grapheme cluster, at most 64 bytes).

remove.description: Takes the author's reaction off instead of putting it on.

to.description: The `msg_id` of the post reacted to.

Reaction.description: One emoji on a message, with who put it there (oldest first).

by.description: The reactors' addresses, as written on their posts.

Registration.description:
How an actor is reachable (ADR-073/081): a local-only actor, a hosted
principal registered privately or publicly, or a remote Hub actor whose
visibility this runtime does not track. Serializes as `local_only`,
`private`, `public`, `registered`.

oneOf.description:
Execute an agent message and stream the response — retired in
the principal-as-single-actor migration (audit C4). The legacy
Execute path went through `StatelessAgentService` directly,
bypassing `PrincipalManager` permission checks, session
creation, and root-agent routing. All chat traffic is now
routed through `PrincipalSend` (one-shot) or
`PrincipalSendStream` (streaming) — both go through
`PrincipalManager::receive` and produce principal-scoped
sessions and audit trails.
Execute a tool synchronously with the calling principal's
identity and session attribution (ADR-061, ADR-066). The synchronous counterpart of
the retired `AsyncSpawn` packet (removed 2026-09-27 with the
dead IPC async-spawn path, ADR-063 (dead IPC path)): same
server-side attribution (the principal is
resolved from `session_key`, its registered catalog is
derived from it server-side — never carried on the wire), but
the handler awaits the result and returns it as
`ResponsePacket::ToolExecuted` instead of a receipt. This is the
callback surface for agent-authored workflow processes
(`sdks/python/peko_workflow`).

`run_token` (phase 2b, ADR-061 D6): the `PEKO_RUN_TOKEN` a
`Workflow` spawn injected into the calling process. When
present it must validate against the daemon's in-memory
registry AND name this packet's `session_key` / principal —
unknown, expired, or mismatched tokens fail closed. When
absent, the pre-2b local-transport trust applies unchanged.

run_token.description:
Optional workflow run token; additive in phase 2b (older
clients never send it, older daemons ignore unknown fields).

Request graceful daemon shutdown
Get system status
Run system doctor

session (ADR-046). For historical events that pre-date the
current daemon process, the CLI falls back to reading the
JSONL file directly via `peko audit tail` — the IPC query
only sees the ring buffer. The CLI's `peko audit list`
subcommand is the primary user of this packet.

event_type_prefix.description:
Optional filter: only return events whose `event_type`
starts with this prefix (e.g. `"cron."`).

limit.description:
Maximum number of entries to return (newest first). The
daemon's ring buffer is bounded (10k entries); requests
above the cap are clipped by the ring buffer.

principal.description:
Optional filter: only return events whose `details.principal_name`
matches (or whose caller is a `ActorRef::Principal` with
this id). The `peko audit tail --principal` flag uses this.

oneOf.description: List all loaded Principals.

Look up a single Principal by name. Returns `ResponsePacket::PrincipalGet`
on hit, or `ResponsePacket::Error` with `principal_not_found` on miss.

Create a new peko (ADR-105). The daemon lays down its folder,
registers it, and schedules its first turn
(`principal::provision`); the caller owns it. `peko create` and
Peko Desktop both send this.

`model_id` is the configured model the principal pins at
creation. It is required: every principal must be created with
a configured model.

The caller showed the seed's setup steps to the person and
they accepted them (ADR-104). A seed that carries setup steps
is refused with `[setup_not_accepted]` and the steps unless
this is true: the new peko runs them on its first turn, as
the owner's OS user.

A seed's TOML text (ADR-060), e.g. downloaded from PekoHub: the
new peko grows from it with a fresh identity, owned by the
caller. `model_id` and `description` override the seed's.

seed_path.description:
A seed file on this computer, read by the daemon, for a seed
too large to travel in one request. Only an operator caller
may name one; ignored when `seed` is given.

oneOf.description:
Load (or no-op when already loaded) a principal that exists on
disk into the daemon's in-memory manager. Used by
`peko principal create` when the daemon is already running:
the CLI materializes the workspace locally, then asks the
daemon to pick it up so the cron engine (which enumerates
loaded principals) can drive its genesis jobs without waiting
for a restart. Idempotent.

Update an existing Principal's mutable config. All fields
except `name` are optional; omitted fields keep their current
values. Requires `ManageSettings` permission on the principal.

avatar.description:
An emoji or short monogram; `""` clears it
(`principal::config::validate_avatar`).

oneOf.description:
Remove a Principal and delete its workspace/data. Requires
`ManageSettings` permission on the principal.

and `kind` filters restrict the listing; missing filters match
everything. Each row is redacted (no material); see
[`CredentialRow`].

desktop's `useCredentialList` (Tauri `credential_list`
command at `peko-desktop/src-tauri/src/commands/settings.rs:301`)
consumes this so Settings → Credentials can paint per-pill
"Key set" indicators and the FirstRunWalkthrough can detect
existing configuration. The CLI `peko credential list` path
reads the vault directly and is unchanged; this handler is
purely the IPC surface.

Fetch the full record for one credential (id, namespace, name,
kind, metadata, timestamps). The `material` field is NOT
included — use [`RequestPacket::CredentialGetMaterial`] for
the secret itself (audit-logged).

Fetch the secret material for a credential. Audit-logged on
the daemon side because the only legitimate caller is the
"Reveal" UI affordance or the rotation-binding test path.

reason.description:
Free-form caller-supplied justification. Logged at INFO
alongside the credential id so an audit trail ties the
reveal back to its purpose.

Live-ping the model identified by `id` and report whether the
endpoint answered. Replaces the pre-migration `CredentialTest`:
validation now happens at the model level (base URL + wire
format + credential), mirroring
`providers::validator::Validator::test`.

plan (ADR-115). The engine listens for the browser's return on
its own loopback port and stores the sign-in in vault slot
`llm/<name>` (default `chatgpt`). The reply carries the address
to open; follow with `chatgpt_sign_in_status`.

How a ChatGPT sign-in is going. `pasted_url` hands it the
address a browser on another computer ended on.
Stop waiting for a ChatGPT sign-in.

Insert or overwrite a credential at `(namespace, name)` with
the given material. The vault assigns a fresh UUID on insert
and returns it in the reply; on overwrite the existing
credential at the slot is replaced (a new id is generated
unless the caller specifies one — see RP3A follow-up if that
path becomes necessary).

[`crate::common::vault::CredentialKind`]. `metadata` is an
optional JSON object holding per-kind extras (OAuth

supplied, every catalog entry that previously referenced the
credential at `replace_on` is rewritten to point at the new
id before the response is sent. Used by
`peko credential set --replace-on <old-id>` for bulk rotation
of dependents. The response's `rewired_models` field reports

material.description:
Raw secret string from the caller. Wrapped in
`SecretString` on the handler side before persisting.

oneOf.description:
Remove a credential by `id`. Powers the desktop's
`credential_delete` Tauri command; the CLI's
`peko credential delete <id>` writes the vault directly.
Mirrors `Vault::delete_credential`.

(the default), the handler refuses to delete a credential
referenced by one or more configured models and emits
`ResponsePacket::Error` with code `credential_in_use` so the
CLI can show a dependents list. When `true`, every catalog
entry that pointed at this credential is detached (`null`)
before the delete; `broken_references` on the response
reports how many entries were detached. Force-deletes are
audit-logged at WARN.

Enumerate every rotation binding currently configured in the
vault. Each binding carries its slot key (`{namespace}:{name}`),
strategy, and ordered list of credential ids.

Fetch one binding by slot key. Returns `None` if no binding
exists for the slot.

Insert or overwrite the rotation binding for a `{namespace}:{name}`
slot. `strategy` is one of `round_robin` (today's only honored
strategy), `last_resort`, or `random` (reserved; the resolver
rejects them with a clear error if encountered). `order` is
the ordered list of credential ids.

Remove a binding by slot key. Returns `Ok(true)` if a binding
was removed.

Re-read the model catalog and the credential vault from
disk. Sent by `peko model {add,remove}` and
`peko credential {set,delete}` so the long-running daemon
observes CLI mutations without a restart.
Legacy preset discovery. Returns an empty preset list (ADR-068).

The chat models an endpoint offers, read from the endpoint
itself with the given key, so a model is chosen without knowing
its id. Nothing is stored.

Add a model using explicit endpoint settings and optional metadata.
Optionally stores a key in the vault in the same round trip.

Update an existing model catalog entry. All fields except
`id` are optional; omitted fields keep their current values.
The daemon persists the merged entry to `models.toml` and
returns the updated catalog-summary view.

Remove a model from the catalog. Returns `removed: true` if
an entry with this id existed. Idempotent — removing a missing
id is not an error.

Read the principal's current quota status (used + limits +

— the daemon's existing trust model is sufficient for F18;
owner-only authz is a follow-up.

to `PeerRegistry`. The `name` field holds the principal name
(default) or the peer id (when `is_peer` is `true`).

limits + cycle). Persists to `peko.toml` and rebuilds
the meter so the new limits take effect on the next call.

`peer.toml` in the peer's directory).

Force-reset the principal's quota meter to a fresh window
without touching the config. Useful for ops/tests.

Register this runtime and its local user with PekoHub (ADR-081
D2/D3) under the account `token` signs in as — an OAuth access token
(pekohub ADR-007) or an API key — then connect the tunnel. Local

conversations with remote pekos are deleted here (ADR-091 D5); with

`answers.to`; `message` is their readable text and must not be
empty.

for a file sent in over HTTP (ADR-121 D5). The engine reads

replies to. The turn reads the start of that message with it.

a caller with the owner's authority. Absent for the caller's
