the full final answer (identical content to what
`PrincipalSend` would have returned). Wire-compatible with the
`principal_send` request shape so the desktop Chat can opt in
to streaming without changing the root agent's behavior.

answers.description:
ADR-114 D1: the message answers the questions of the post
`answers.to`; `message` is their readable text and must not be
empty.

attachments.description:
ADR-088: absolute paths of files to attach, or `upload:<id>`
for a file sent in over HTTP (ADR-121 D5). The engine reads
them itself, so only the local operator (or an `owner` key)
may attach.

reply_to.description:
ADR-126 D6: the `msg_id` of the post in the DM this message
replies to. The turn reads the start of that message with it.

send_as.description:
ADR-113 D7: the visitor this message is from, vouched for by
a caller with the owner's authority. Absent for the caller's
own message.

oneOf.description:
Soft-stop the run bound to a (principal, peer) thread.

The stop complement to `PrincipalSend`/`PrincipalSendStream`:
the server resolves the peer's child session, fires the run's
cancel token (the agentic loop exits at the next iteration
boundary), posts a `⏹ stopped by user` marker to the peer's DM
channel, and leaves a stop-context note in the session inbox
for the next run. `peer: None` means the principal's owner
thread. The server enforces the same privacy rule as
`PrincipalLog` (`caller == peer || caller == principal.owner`).
Idempotent: no in-flight run ⇒ `Done { success: false,
error: "no running turn…" }` so the CLI can print a notice and
exit 0.

main.description:
Stop the turn in the peko's main session instead of a
conversation (ADR-104 D5): its first-turn setup, its
keepalive, or scheduled work. Owner only; `peer` is ignored.
A stopped first turn is over: it is not run again.

oneOf.description:
The approval requests waiting for a principal's owner (ADR-078 D7).
Owner (or operator) only.

How a peko's first turn is going (ADR-104 D4): whether it is
still setting itself up, what it has done so far, and its setup
report once written. Owner (or operator) only.

Run a peko's setup steps again (ADR-106): a setup turn that
checks each step and carries out the ones that do not work yet.
Owner (or operator) only. Answers `done`; `success: false` when
the peko lists no steps, a setup turn is already scheduled, or it
is still on its first turn.

The owner's decision on approval request `id`: approve (with
`always`, also add an always-allow rule to `POLICY.md`) or deny.
The owner's own action — the desktop's buttons, `peko approve` /
`peko deny` — never a message a model reads. Owner (or operator)
only.

A peko's secrets and the secret requests waiting for its owner
(ADR-116 D3): names only, never values. Owner only, local callers
only. Answered with `SecretList`.

The owner's value for secret request `id` (a `sec_…` id, or the
name of a waiting request), or for a new peko secret named `id`
when none waits (ADR-116 D3). The value goes to the vault and is
in no response. Owner only, local callers only. Answered with
`SecretDone`.

The owner declines secret request `id`. Owner only, local callers
only. Answered with `SecretDone`.

Remove peko secret `secret`. Owner only, local callers only.
Answered with `SecretDone`.

One thing a viewer asks of a peko's browser (ADR-119 D4–D6):
`state`, `frame`, `control`, `input`, `open`, `stop` for peko
`name`; or, with no peko, `status` (is there a browser to start)
and `install` (download the runtime's own). Owner only, local
callers only. Answered with `BrowserResult`.

Whether a peko is using this computer's screen, doing what, and
whether the owner's hand paused it (ADR-123 D5), with the
system's grants. Peko Desktop asks while it runs, to show its
indicator. Local callers only. Answered with `ComputerResult`.

**Let it continue** (ADR-123 D2): lift the pause the owner's input
put on the run using the screen, and wake its session. Local
callers only. Answered with `ComputerResult`.

**Stop** (ADR-123 D5): end the run using the screen, wherever it
runs (a conversation, cron, the keepalive). Local callers only.
Answered with `ComputerResult`.

Ask the system for the grants `Computer` needs (ADR-123 D5): on
macOS, opens the Screen Recording and Accessibility prompts for the
app that started the engine. Local callers only. Answered with
`ComputerResult`.

Recent turns of a peko that changed files, newest first (ADR-117):
those in `channel` when given, or with `dm`, in the DM of `peer`
(the caller when absent) as `principal_log` resolves it. Owner
only, local callers only. Answered with `TurnChanges`.

Undo turn `turn`'s file changes (ADR-117 D3). Owner only, local
callers only. Answered with `TurnUndone`.

Read a peer's conversation thread with a Principal.

This is the read complement to `PrincipalSend`. There is no
`peko session` CLI command (ADR-042): peers only ever see their
own thread, the owner sees their own by default, and any
other-thread read by the owner requires `peer` to be set
explicitly. The server enforces the privacy check (`caller ==
peer || caller == principal.owner`) plus the principal's `Chat`
grant before returning anything.

author.description:
Optional exact author filter (the raw channel-log author —
a peer ActorRef wire form or the principal's id).

cursor.description:
Opaque pagination cursor from a previous `PrincipalLog`
response's `next_cursor`. `None` reads the latest page.
Malformed cursors and cursors bound to another thread are
rejected with `bad_cursor`.

limit.description: Cap on number of messages returned (default 50, max 1000).

query.description:
Optional case-insensitive substring filter on message text.
Applied while paging (the daemon keeps walking older pages
until the page fills or the log is exhausted).

since_secs.description: Only messages newer than `now() - since_secs` are returned.

oneOf.description:
What a peko's visitors reach (ADR-113), for a sharing screen:
`[visitors]` and each person's own section of its `ACCESS.toml`,
the MCP servers it has, and the people it has talked with. Owner
only. Answered with `PrincipalAccess`.

Replace what visitors reach: `visitors` for everyone, and
`people` as the whole set of per-person sections (one left out is
removed). The file keeps its comments and `own` settings; nothing
is written unless the result is valid. Owner only. Answered with
`PrincipalAccess` as the file now is.

Follow everything a peko posts in its one-to-one conversations
(owner only): one `PrincipalSentAppended` per post, naming whom it
went to, with `Heartbeat` ticks between. For a script that
relays a peko's conversations to another service, so a message
the peko sends later (after its owner approves a request, say)
reaches the person too. `since` (RFC 3339) first replays the
peko's posts newer than it, oldest first; without it the stream
starts now. No `Done`: it ends when the client goes away.

Watch a peer's conversation thread with a Principal: replay
`Posted` events newer than `since_cursor`, then stream new
messages live.

The privacy-checked sibling of `ChannelEventsWatch` (ADR-042):
the server resolves `(name, peer)` to the peer's DM channel and
enforces the same rule as `PrincipalLog` (`caller == peer ||
caller == principal.owner`, plus the `Chat` grant). The
response is a stream of `PrincipalLogAppended` packets
interleaved with `Heartbeat` ticks (every
`HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECS`) so a quiet thread never trips the
client's per-packet idle timeout. No `Done` on close — the
stream ends when the client disconnects or the daemon shuts
down.

`since_cursor` reuses the log command's line-number cursor:
only rows with line number greater than the cursor replay.
`None` replays the whole thread.

since_cursor.description:
Replay seed — rows strictly newer than this line-number
cursor. `None` replays from the start.

rotate_keys.description:
Import as a new actor: fresh keys, DID, actor key and local ID
(ADR-081 D6 step 1).

oneOf.description: Preview a `.peko` package before importing it.

rotate_keys.description:
Without it, a snapshot of an actor hosted here is refused at
preview, before the inventory is shown.

oneOf.description:
Transfer a principal to a new owner (ADR-081 D4). Only the current
owner may transfer; an online principal's new owner must be a Hub
actor.

Set the live status of a Principal's tunnel instance. Persisted to
`peko.toml` so the change survives daemon restart. Delegates
to `TunnelDispatcher::set_instance_status` to publish a
`status_update` to the hub.

Set the exposure of a Principal's tunnel instance. Persisted to
`peko.toml` so the change survives daemon restart. Delegates
to `TunnelDispatcher::set_instance_exposure` to publish an
`exposure_update` to the hub.

PR #11: mint an invite token for this principal. The caller
supplies the desired `scope` (one or more `Permission` values)
and the TTL in seconds. The runtime returns the encoded token
plus its claims so the CLI/desktop can render the share URL.

PR #11: revoke an invite token by `jti`. Idempotent — revoking
an unknown `jti` is a no-op (returns success).

Create a new group channel owned by `creator_name` (DMs are
opened by `ChannelSend`, ADR-082).

`id` (ADR-049 Phase 2, D5) is the optional explicit channel id
(e.g. `group:<slug>`), validated by the handler via
`ChannelId::parse`. Serde-defaulted so pre-Phase-2 clients
decode as `None` (the store mints a fresh `chan_<8 base36>`).
Add `invitee_name` to `channel` (invited by `inviter_name`).

Post a message to `channel` from `sender_name`. `parent` is
the optional task_id of the message being replied to.

ADR-057: user identities are never carried on the wire. The
caller's own attribution identity is derived server-side from
the connection (`CallerContext::attribution_subject`).
`sender_name` is `None` ("speak as my own identity") or a
principal name — a runtime-hosted actor operated by the
caller. A `user:<id>` sender is refused with `[forbidden]`.

answers.description:
ADR-114 D1, D5: the post answers the questions of the post
`answers.to` (a root post: `parent` is refused with it).

attachments.description:
ADR-094: files to send with the post, as absolute paths on
this host; only the local user may attach. Each is copied into
the channel's file store; in a conversation with anyone on
another runtime or the Hub the bytes cross PekoHub, at most
10 MB a file and 25 MB a message.

model.description:
ADR-097 D2: a configured model of the peko's host to answer
this post with, recorded on the post (`Posted.model`). Only the
local user may set it; the host honours it only for the peko's
owner.

react.description:
ADR-126 D1: an emoji reaction on the post `react.to` instead
of a message; `text` and `parent` are ignored with it.

reply_to.description:
ADR-126 D6: the `msg_id` of the post this replies to, in place
of the line-number `parent`.

oneOf.description:
List events for `channel` since `since` (None = from start).

ADR-057: the reader's identity is derived server-side from the
connection (`CallerContext::attribution_subject`) — local and
pekohub JWT callers are always membership-gated as themselves;
API-key callers carry no user identity and stay ungated
(matching their previous no-requester posture).

author.description:
Search mode: exact `Posted` author match (wire form, e.g.
`user:alice`).

before.description:
Line-number cursor bounding the tail read from above
(events strictly older than this line). Ignored unless
`tail` is set.

query.description:
Search mode: case-insensitive substring match on `Posted`
text. When `query` or `author` is set, the daemon runs
`ChannelPort::search` (backward filtered scan; `tail` acts
as the match cap, `before` as the scan anchor) instead of
peeking.

tail.description:
Tail-read mode: return the newest `tail` events at or before
`before` instead of the full forward walk from `since`.
Maps to `ChannelPort::peek_tail`. When absent the legacy
forward `since` semantics apply.

oneOf.description:
PR-2b: subscribe to live events for `channel`. The daemon
replays events from `since` (None = from start) as a series of
`ChannelEventReceived` packets, then holds the connection open
and forwards new events as they arrive (signalled by the
dispatcher after `append_remote_event` succeeds). The stream
closes when the client disconnects or the daemon shuts down.

Wire-compatible with the chat's `PrincipalSendStream` shape
(request → stream of packets → `Done` on close) so the
desktop Tauri backend can reuse the existing stream-forwarding
path that already emits `peko-stream` events for the chat.

ADR-057: the reader's identity is derived server-side from the
connection — same caller-derived membership gate as
`ChannelPeek`.
List members of `channel`.
List channels where `principal_name` is a member.

Remove `principal_name` from `channel` (operator callers;
answers `channel_left`), or, with no `principal_name`, the
caller themself — a person leaving a group (answers
`channel_member_left`).

Copy a Runtime-tier channel into the Shared tier (PR-3d).
Authority gate (`channel:write_shared`) is enforced by the
daemon handler; the in-process CLI fallback path performs
the same check via `RuntimeAuthority`.

A channel's kind, name, members, and how each peko hosted here
wakes in it (ADR-082). Members only, like `ChannelPeek`.

Open, or find, the local user's DM with the peko named by `hub_id`,
hosted on another runtime (ADR-090 D2). `hub_id` is its PekoHub ID
or `@owner/name`; the answer's `hub_id` is always the ID. The
runtime resolves it through PekoHub — with `token`, the caller's
PekoHub access token, when given (used for that one request and
never stored), else with the runtime's own proof, which PekoHub
answers as the runtime's person — and invites it over the tunnel.
Then post and read with `channel_post` / `channel_peek` /
`channel_events_watch`. Local callers only. Answered with
`channel_remote_dm_opened`.

Open, or find, a DM with another person, whose PekoHub account is
`account` (ADR-095 D6). The first time, the person gets a message
request; posts wait in this copy until they accept. Local callers
only; answered with `channel_person_dm_opened`.

name.description: What to call them here until their runtime says.

oneOf.description:
This runtime's person's DMs with other people (ADR-095 D6). Local
callers only; answered with `channel_person_dms_result`.

This runtime's person's DMs with pekos on other runtimes, the ones
opened here and the ones that followed them from their other
computers (ADR-090, ADR-095 D5). Local callers only; answered with
`channel_peko_dms_result`.

The people asking this runtime's person to DM (ADR-095 D6), newest
first. Local callers only; answered with `channel_dm_requests_result`.

Answer a DM request (ADR-095 D6): `accept`, `decline`, or `block`.
Accepting opens the DM and tells the asker's runtime; declining and
blocking tell nobody. Local callers only; answered with
`channel_person_dm_opened` on accept, else `Done`.

Block (`blocked: true`) or unblock a person by PekoHub account
(ADR-095 D6). Local callers only; answered with
`channel_blocked_people`.

The people this runtime's person blocked. Local callers only;
answered with `channel_blocked_people`.

Scroll-back in a DM with a remote peko (ADR-091 D4): the page of
posts before `before` (a `msg_id`), from the peko's host. Not
stored on this runtime. Local callers only; answered with
`ChannelHistoryPage`.

The models the peko in `channel` — this account's DM with one of
its pekos on another runtime — can answer its owner with, from the
peko's host (ADR-097 D1). Local callers only; answered with
`ChannelPekoModelsResult`.

The approval requests waiting for you, the owner of the peko in
`channel` — this account's DM with one of its pekos on another
runtime — from the peko's host (ADR-099 D1). Local callers only;
answered with `ChannelPekoApprovalsResult`.

Your decision on approval request `id` of the peko in `channel`,
applied by its host as `approval_decide` (ADR-099 D2). The owner's
own action — the desktop's buttons — never a message. Local
callers only; answered with `ApprovalDecided`.

One thing you ask of the browser of the peko in `channel`, your
DM with a peko on another of your computers (ADR-119 D6): `verb`
is `state`, `frame`, `control`, `input` or `open`, carried out by
its host. Local callers only; answered with `BrowserResult`.

The groups inviting this runtime's person (ADR-092 D2), newest
first. Local callers only; answered with `ChannelInvitationsResult`.

The groups this runtime's person joined from other runtimes
(ADR-092 D2). Local callers only; answered with
`ChannelPersonGroupsResult`.

Join a group by its invite link, or a public one by its ID
(ADR-092 D5): PekoHub says where it lives, and its home decides.
Local callers only; answered with `ChannelGroupJoined` once the
request is on its way (the group arrives with the home's roster).
With `peko` (a name or local id of a peko the caller owns), that
peko joins, for itself (ADR-098 D2); without, the person does.

Register a group with PekoHub, or change who may find it
(ADR-092 D5), at its home and as its owner peko. Only that peko's
owner; answered with `ChannelGroupRegistered`.

Make an invite link to a registered group good for `days` (default
7, at most 30), or with `revoke` stop every link (ADR-092 D5). As
for `ChannelGroupRegister`; answered with `ChannelGroupLinkResult`.

Set what starts a turn for `principal_name` in a group
(`human` / `mention` / `off`, ADR-082 D3). Groups only — a DM
always wakes on human posts — and only the peko's owner.

ADR-101: read a group's board, or change it with `op` first. The
change is posted as `sender_name` (a peko the caller operates) or,
when absent, as the caller. Groups only. Answered with
`ChannelBoardResult`.
The posts in `channel` not yet delivered to a member on another
runtime (that runtime has been away since, e.g. asleep), by
`msg_id`. Members only. Answered with `ChannelUndeliveredResult`.

ADR-111 D3: show a code that adds a device to this account (a
phone scans it, another computer types it): single use, ten
minutes. Local callers only; this computer must be on its account's
list. Answered with `DeviceCodeShown`.

ADR-111 D3: join this computer to its account's devices with a code
shown on a device already on them. Answers `done` once the device
list has this computer on it (up to two minutes). Local callers only.

ADR-111: this account's devices, whether this computer is on them,
and what waits for the owner about the account (owner changes,
pekos' new identities, contacts' devices that start over). Local
callers only. Answered with `DeviceListResult`.

ADR-125 D9: how this computer connects to its other computers and
people's, and the path to each (`direct`, `relay`, `waiting`,
`offline`). Local callers only. Answered with `NetworkStatusResult`.

ADR-125 D9: set any of the `[network]` link settings; writes
`runtime.toml` and applies them at once (starts or stops the
listener, closes links no longer admitted, tells peers whether
this computer takes relayed frames). An absent field is left as it
is; an empty `direct_listen` goes back to the default. Local
callers only. Answered with `NetworkStatusResult`.

ADR-125 D9: dial a computer's known addresses now (every one's,
without `runtime_id`), without waiting for the backoff. Local
callers only. Answered with `Done`.

ADR-112: the code of an identity as this computer holds it, to
compare with its owner's: `account`, `user:hub:<id>`,
`peko:hub:<id>`, or one of your pekos by name or id. Local callers
only. Answered with `IdentityCodeResult` (`code` absent when this
computer holds no identity for it yet).

ADR-111 D4: remove a device from the account (by its id, or a
phone's Hub id); every computer stops acting on it. Local callers
only. Answers `done`.

ADR-111 D6: decide one of `device_list`'s `security` requests.
Local callers only. Answered with `ApprovalDecided`.

ADR-108 D5: the person has seen `channel` up to a post. Name it by
`msg_id`, or give `at` (RFC 3339) for the newest post at or before
that time, which is what a client that shows a thread by time
knows. Exactly one of the two. Moves their read mark forward (never
back) and tells their other computers. Local callers only. Answered
with `ChannelReadMarked`.

ADR-108 D5: the person's read mark and unread count in each of
their conversations. Local callers only. Answered with
`ChannelReadStateResult`.
Streaming text chunk

Synchronous tool-execution result (ADR-061 phase 1) — the reply
to `RequestPacket::ExecuteTool`. Carries the F37 funnel triplet
(`tool_result_from_hook`): `content` is the display string the
agentic loop would feed the model, `result` the structured
value, and `success` is false for tool errors AND
capability-gate denials alike (the fail-closed path surfaces as
data, not a transport error). Payloads that would exceed the
datagram budget arrive with `truncated: true`, `content` clipped
to fit (marker appended) and `result` dropped to null.
Final success/failure marker
Error response
Ping response
Heartbeat — sent during long streams so CLI can detect dead daemon
Shutdown acknowledgement

Cron job list response
Channel created — returns the new `ChannelId`.

Invite acknowledged. ADR-049 Phase 1: the invitee is
`ActorRef`-typed (a principal or a `user:<id>` user).
Post acknowledged — returns the new task id.
Peek result — full event list since the requested cursor.

event_ids.description:
Line-number ids parallel to `events` (the source line each
event was read from). Lets watch-style consumers advance a
`since` cursor precisely instead of re-reading the whole
log on every poll. Empty when the serving daemon predates
the field.

has_more.description:
Tail reads only: true when the log holds events older than
the first returned one (page further back with `before`).

older_elsewhere.description:
ADR-095 D1: this computer's copy of the person's DM with a
remote peko doesn't reach the conversation's first post yet,
so older posts may be read from the peko's copy
(`channel_history_older`). False for every other channel and
once the copy is complete.

reactions.description:
ADR-126 D1: the reactions on the returned posts, by `msg_id`
(posts with none are left out). Reaction posts stay in
`events`, so a cursor still advances past them; a client shows
them on their message, not as messages
(`ChannelEvent::is_message`).

resume_before.description:
Search mode only: the oldest line the scan examined. Pass
back as `before` to continue searching older history.
`None` when the scan reached the top of the log.

oneOf.description:
PR-2b: one event in a `ChannelEventsWatch` stream. The daemon
emits one of these per event — first replaying events from the
`since` cursor, then forwarding new events as they arrive. The
stream closes with `Done { request_id }` when the client
disconnects or the daemon shuts down.

Members list. ADR-049 Phase 1: members are `ActorRef`-typed
(principals and users).

member_provenance.description:
P1.2 attribution: per-member runtime provenance (`runtime_id
= None` for local members). Default empty so pre-PR-3b
consumers that don't read this field see no change to the
wire shape.

oneOf.description: List of channels where the principal is a member.

Leave acknowledged — `principal` is no longer a member of
`channel`.

Response to a `ChannelLeave` without `principal_name`: the
caller (`member`) left the group.

Shared-tier pin acknowledged. `shared_path` is the absolute
Shared root the channel directory was copied to. The Runtime
source dir remains (COPY semantics — see PR-3d plan).
Response to `ChannelInfo`.

created_at.description:
When the group (or DM) began: the home's time, not when this
copy was made (ADR-092 D1).

group.description: A group's home and PekoHub registration (ADR-092 D1/D5).

pekos.description:
The member pekos hosted on this runtime and their wake
policy. A DM's is always `human`; a group binding not yet
written reads as the group default, `mention`.

people.description:
Everyone in it, once each, with their names: the members here,
those reached through other runtimes, and the creator. Every
form a member appears as (in the roster or as a post's author)
is one of their `aliases`, so a reader names them all.

oneOf.description: Response to `ChannelPersonGroups` (ADR-092 D2).

Response to `ChannelGroupJoin` (ADR-092 D5): the request is on its
way to the group's home.
Response to `ChannelGroupRegister` (ADR-092 D5).

id.description: The group's PekoHub ID, a bare number.

oneOf.description:
Response to `ChannelGroupLink` (ADR-092 D5): the new link and its
expiry (RFC 3339), or how many links `revoke` stopped.
Response to `ChannelInvitations` (ADR-092 D2).

Response to `ChannelPekoModels` (ADR-097 D1): the host's enabled
models, by configured id and name; empty when the host offers none
to this person.

Response to `ChannelPekoApprovals` (ADR-099 D1): the requests
waiting on the peko's host, oldest first, as `approval_list`
reports them; empty when the host shows this person none.

Response to `ChannelHistoryOlder` (ADR-091 D4): posts, oldest
first, and whether older ones remain on the host.
Response to `ChannelOpenRemoteDm` (ADR-090 D2).

created.description: Whether this request created the DM.

name.description: The peko's name, when PekoHub gave one.

oneOf.description:
Response to `ChannelOpenPersonDm`, and to accepting a DM request
(ADR-095 D6).

created.description: Whether this request created the DM here.

oneOf.description: Response to `ChannelPersonDms` (ADR-095 D6).
Response to `ChannelPekoDms`.
Response to `ChannelDmRequests` (ADR-095 D6).

Response to `ChannelBlockPerson` / `ChannelBlocked`: everyone
blocked now, `user:hub:<account>`.

names.description:
What each is called here, when known (their request named
them).

oneOf.description:
Response to `ChannelBoard` (ADR-101): the board's items worth
showing (everything not done, and what was done in the last day),
in the order they were added. Each item carries its full `id` and
its `short` reference.
Response to `ChannelUndelivered`: undelivered posts by `msg_id`,
oldest first; empty when everything arrived.

Response to `DeviceAdd` (ADR-111 D3): the code to show
(`ABCD-EFGH-JKMN`), and the same as QR text. Shown on this
computer's screen and nowhere else.
Response to `DeviceList` (ADR-111), oldest device first.

account.description: `user:hub:<id>`, absent when this computer is not registered.

code.description: ADR-112: the account's code, once this computer holds its list.

on_list.description:
Whether this computer is on its account's devices. While it is not,
`devices` is the list PekoHub shows, for reference only.

oneOf.description: Response to `NetworkStatus` and `NetworkSettingsSet` (ADR-125 D9).

direct_listen.description:
The settings as written (for an editor of them): `direct_listen`
(absent: the default), `direct_addresses`, `direct_peers`.

oneOf.description: Response to `IdentityCode` (ADR-112).

Response to `ChannelMarkRead` (ADR-108 D5): whether the mark
moved (`false` when it already covered that post, or the post has
not arrived here yet).
Response to `ChannelReadState` (ADR-108 D5).
Response to `ChannelSetWake`: the policy now stored.

Quota status snapshot (F18). Carries the principal's live
`QuotaState` — used counters, configured limits (via the
cycle), and the current window's start/end timestamps.
Returned for `QuotaGet`, `QuotaSet`, and `QuotaReset`.

config.description:
The principal's effective `QuotaConfig`. Mirrors the

Newest-first list of audit events matching the query.

Result of `PrincipalCreate`. Returns the new principal's
summary so the caller can render it without a follow-up
`PrincipalList`. Past-tense pairing with `PrincipalCreate`.

Result of `PrincipalUpdate`. Echoes the updated principal's

Result of `PrincipalRemove`. `removed` is `true` when the
principal existed and was deleted; idempotent removes return

Result of `PrincipalReload`. `loaded` is `true` when the

Result of `CredentialList`. One row per provider id that the

Field names mirror the desktop's `CredentialRow`

Reply to [`RequestPacket::ModelTest`]. Carries the
structured outcome so the UI can render latency + reason
without re-parsing strings. `tested_at` is an ISO-8601 UTC
stamp the validator computes at response-build time so
callers don't have to read the daemon's wall clock.

Reply to [`RequestPacket::CredentialSet`]. The vault write
has already succeeded (or surfaced an error via
[`ResponsePacket::Error`]) by the time this is sent. The
`id` echo lets the desktop update its local UI without
re-issuing a `credential_list` round-trip.

`rewired_models` (PR 3 / `feature/model-first-config`):
count of catalog entries that were rebound from the
previous credential id (passed via
`CredentialSet::replace_on`) to this new id. Zero on a plain
set; the CLI's `--replace-on` flow surfaces this count so
the user sees "Rewired N models: …" without a follow-up
`model list` round-trip.

Reply to [`RequestPacket::CredentialDelete`]. See
[`ResponsePacket::CredentialSetDone`] for the same notes on
the success/error split.

`broken_references` (PR 3 / `feature/model-first-config`):
count of catalog entries that pointed at this credential
and were detached (`credential_id = null`) before the
delete. Zero on a normal delete; non-zero on a `--force`
delete. The CLI surfaces this count so the user sees
"Removed credential. Detached N model(s)." without a
follow-up `model list` round-trip.

Reply to `chatgpt_sign_in_status` and `chatgpt_sign_in_cancel`.

account.description: The Hub account the runtime and its local user now belong to.

The Hub account the local user is linked to (ADR-081 D3), as
its UUID: the local user is also `user:hub:<account>`. Absent
when unregistered, and from older daemons.

That account's name as Hub gave it at registration (its
display name, else its handle).

connection.description:
ADR-125: how this computer connects (`pekohub`, `automatic`,
`direct`). Absent from older daemons.

hub_url.description:
The hub this runtime is registered with (`https://pekohub.ai`);
absent when unregistered, and from older daemons.

person_handle.description: Their PekoHub handle, while signed in (ADR-124).

What this computer's person is called (ADR-124): their PekoHub
name when signed in, else the name they chose here, else their

oneOf.description:
Comprehensive daemon status payload (issue #8). Includes tunnel
health snapshot suitable for `peko daemon status --json`.

`mode` is added by the engine-adoption work (ADR-043): clients
like `peko-desktop`'s SidecarSupervisor use it to detect when a
foreign daemon (CLI-launched or another sidecar) is already
holding the IPC socket, instead of trying to spawn a competing
child. `#[serde(default)]` makes the field forward+backward
compatible: old clients ignore it, old daemons omit it.

Non-streaming result of `PrincipalSend`. Single packet with the
root agent's final answer.

Streaming chunk of a `PrincipalSendStream` response. The daemon
emits zero or more of these as the root agent agent produces
assistant text. The frontend appends each `delta` to the
in-flight assistant message.

Content-free agentic-iteration boundary marker for a
`PrincipalSendStream` response. Emitted once at the start of each
agentic loop iteration (when the runtime observes a
`Lifecycle{Running}` event). Clients use it to break assistant
text into one bubble per iteration and to show a "working"
indicator while awaiting the next iteration's first token
(e.g. during a tool call between iterations). `iteration` is
1-based. Tool-call / thinking detail is intentionally NOT sent —
it stays backend-only in the session log.

Final packet of a `PrincipalSendStream` response. Carries the
full final answer (same content the non-streaming `PrincipalSent`
would have returned) so the frontend can confirm the response
and persist it. Always followed by a `Done` packet. `options`
are the suggested replies posted with the answer (ADR-093) and
`ask` the questions it asks (ADR-114), each omitted when none.

Run-summary packet emitted by the daemon at the end of a
principal-send run. Aggregates the run's tool-call errors and
cumulative token usage so thin consumers that don't persist the
session JSONL can surface
these facts to the user.

Always emitted between `PrincipalSent*` / `PrincipalSentDone` /
`PrincipalSent` and the final `Done` packet on both Streaming
and OneShot response kinds. Consumers that don't know about
this variant should treat it as opaque (their `_ => {}`
fallthrough already swallows it). All fields are
`#[serde(default)]` so old CLIs tolerate a daemon that emits
them and old daemons don't crash when deserializing CLI
commands that include them in the future.

`iterations` is the count of `Lifecycle{Running}` events
observed by the daemon — i.e. the number of agentic-loop turns
the LLM ran. `usage` is the cumulative token usage across all
turns (peko-engine emits one `AgenticEvent::Usage` per run,
immediately before `Lifecycle{End}`). `tool_errors` records
every `ToolEnd { success: false }` event seen during the run,
correlated against the most recent `ToolStart` for the same
`tool_id` so the user sees `"<tool_name>: <error_msg>"`.

A tool call started in a streaming send's run. `input` is a
short redacted summary of the arguments, sent only when the
caller is the peko's owner (results and arguments can carry the
owner's private context).

A tool call finished. `output` is a short redacted excerpt of
the result, owner only, like `input`.

A thinking (reasoning) text delta. Owner only: thinking can
quote the prompt's private sections.

Successor packet emitted when a steering message was queued
during the final-iteration drain of `PrincipalSendStream` and
the predecessor's run has now completed. The runtime drained
the pending steering, started a fresh run for it, and is now
delivering the answer. `predecessor_request_id` is the
original `request_id` of the streamed send; `request_id` is the
fresh id of the successor run (returned so the client can
correlate if it wants to steer the new run). Multiple
`PrincipalSentSuccessor` packets may follow the predecessor's
`PrincipalSentDone`; each carries the full content of one
drained steering item. The original `Done { request_id:
predecessor_request_id, success: true }` closes the original
stream after the successors have been delivered.

Response to a `PrincipalLog` request. Returns one bounded page of
the peer's DM-channel conversation for `(principal_did, peer)` —
`messages` ordered oldest-to-newest, `next_cursor` opaque
for paging older pages, and `has_more` true when more pages
exist. Pre-launch clean cutover: no `session_id`, no
`HistoryEvent`s, no session-internal vocabulary. Errors emit
`Error { code, message }` with `code` in
`"not_found" | "forbidden" | "bad_cursor" | "internal_error"`.

reacts on it (`channel_post` `react`). Absent from older daemons.

The conversation's last run failed (ADR-089 D5): shown beside
it, never written into it. Absent once a run succeeds, after a

`provisioned` | `defined` | `genesis_pending` | `organized`.
Anything but `organized` means the first turn is not over.

The peko's own report (`kb/setup.md`), once it wrote one;
at most 16 KiB.

Each setup step with its result, in order, read from the

Whether a turn is running in the main session right now, so
`principal_stop` with `main` has something to stop.

Where setup stands (ADR-106): `none` (no steps listed),
`pending` (some steps not reported, nothing scheduled),

What the owner's decision did (`message`: e.g. "Approved apr_…
Running it for … now").

A peko's recent turns that changed files (ADR-117).
What undoing a turn did: files put back, and files left alone.

The answer to a `browser` request (ADR-119). A `frame` names the

The answer to `computer_state`, `computer_resume`, `computer_stop`

What `secret_provide` / `secret_decline` / `secret_delete` did.

One message on a `PrincipalLogWatch` stream — a replayed or

A peko's visitor rules (`principal_access_get` / `_set`).

The people and pekos it has had one-to-one conversations

The peko's workspace, absolute on this computer: the paths in

Result of previewing a `.peko` package before import.

An online principal's transfer became an offer (ADR-081 D4,

Result of `PrincipalSetStatus`. Echoes the persisted status so

Result of `PrincipalRegister`. Echoes the persisted exposure.

PR #11: result of `PrincipalMintInvite`. Returns the wire

What a sharing screen edits of one section of `ACCESS.toml`: the

Status.description:
Persisted live status for a Principal's tunnel instance.

Principal-owned mirror of `tunnel::protocol::InstanceStatus`; converted at
the tunnel edge. `None` at the `PrincipalConfig` level means the daemon's
runtime state is the source of truth.

ThinkingEffort.description:
Reasoning-effort knob surfaced to callers (F25).

Each adapter maps this onto its provider-native field:
- OpenAI Chat Completions: `body["reasoning_effort"] = "low"|"medium"|"high"`
- OpenAI Responses:        `body["reasoning"] = {effort, summary}`
- Anthropic:               `thinking: {type:"adaptive"}` + `output_config`
                           for Opus 4-6+ / Sonnet 5 / Fable 5+, otherwise
                           `thinking: {type:"enabled", budget_tokens: N}`
                           with an effort→budget mapping
                           (low→1024, medium→4096, high→32_000).

`None` means "do not request reasoning" (default — most callers
won't have reasoning enabled). `Adaptive` is honored only on
adapters that detect adaptive-capable model ids; others fall
back to a `High` budget mapping.
`XHigh` and `Max` map to OpenAI's wire vocabulary (`"xhigh"`,
`"max"`) but are silently clamped on adapters that don't yet
support them.

On the wire (catalog, IPC) a level is its lowercase name: `none`,
`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`, `adaptive`.

ThinkingFormat.description:
Per-provider thinking-reasoning wire shape (F29).

Each variant maps `ChatOptions::thinking_effort` (F25) onto the
provider-native field the adapter emits on the request body.
`OpenAi`, `Anthropic`, and `OpenAiResponses` mirror the F25
adapter defaults — they are listed here so a single
`ProviderCompat` annotation can drive per-adapter emit even for
providers that already work today.

The specialty variants cover providers whose `extra_body.thinking`
shape is documented but unique (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Zai) plus
OpenRouter / Together whose reasoning namespace differs from
canonical OpenAI's. Wire shapes:

| Variant           | Wire field                                         |
|-------------------|----------------------------------------------------|
| `OpenAi`          | `body["reasoning_effort"] = "low\|medium\|high"`    |
| `Anthropic`       | `thinking: {type, budget_tokens}` (budget) or     |
|                   | `thinking: {type:"adaptive"}` + `output_config`    |
|                   | (adaptive on Opus 4-6+ / Sonnet 5 / Fable 5+)      |
| `OpenAiResponses` | `body["reasoning"] = {effort, summary}` +          |
|                   | `include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]`         |
| `Kimi`            | `extra_body.thinking = {type, effort, keep}` on    |
|                   | the Anthropic-shaped wire (kimi-code `anthropic.ts:392-462`) |
| `DeepSeek`        | `extra_body.thinking = {type:"enabled"}` +          |
|                   | canonical `reasoning_effort`                       |
| `Qwen`            | `extra_body.enable_thinking = bool` (toggle only)  |
| `Zai`             | `thinking: {type, clear_thinking}` — Anthropic-    |
|                   | compat; `clear_thinking: "20251015"` matches the   |
|                   | Anthropic `clear_thinking_20251015` pattern (F27)  |
| `OpenRouter`      | `reasoning: {effort: "low\|medium\|high"}`         |
| `Together`        | `reasoning: {enabled: bool}` (no effort levels)    |

ToolErrorEntry.description:
One tool-call error observed during a run, surfaced on
`ResponsePacket::RunSummary`. `tool_name` is the name as it
appeared on the most recent `ToolStart` event for the same
`tool_id`; missing when no `ToolStart` was seen before the
failure (the runtime still records the error so users can see
`success: false` regardless). `error_message` is the
short-truncated error text the tool returned in `result`.

TurnSummary.description: A turn as shown (`Changes` tool, IPC `turn_changes`).

shell.description: It ran shell commands: changes outside the workspace aren't listed.

UndoSkipped.description: A file undo left alone (ADR-117 D3).

path.description: Relative to the peko's workspace when inside it.

why.description: `changed since`, or why its earlier version can't be put back.

WakePolicy.description:
What starts a turn for a bound principal (ADR-082 D3). Whatever the
policy, a principal-authored post or a reply never does (ADR-072).

oneOf.description: Every human (user or visitor) root post. A DM's fixed policy.
A human root post mentioning `@<name>`. A group's default.
Nothing; posts wait for `ChannelRead` or the unread summary.

description: Every request a client sends the engine (`RequestPacket`) and every packet it answers with (`ResponsePacket`), over the local socket or the HTTP door (`POST /v1/call`, ADR-121). `AuthenticatedRequest` is a request as the socket carries it, with an optional `auth` header beside its fields. Over HTTP `request_id` may be left out. Each variant's `x-stability` is `stable` (breaks only in a minor version, ADR-102) or `internal` (may change in a patch). Generated from the Rust types: do not edit by hand.
